name: Solar Crop Drying
summary: Improved solar dryers that use captured solar heat to dry agricultural produce rapidly and hygienically, reducing aflatoxin contamination and post-harvest losses.
description: Solar drying technology uses solar radiation — either direct or via a solar collector — to dry agricultural produce more rapidly and hygienically than traditional open sun drying on the ground. Indirect solar dryers channel heated air over produce on mesh trays inside an enclosed drying chamber, protecting produce from dust, rain, insects, and animals. Direct solar dryers use transparent plastic or glass covers on drying beds. In Uganda, solar drying is used extensively for coffee (raised bed drying), fish, cassava, vegetables, and herbs. Improved solar dryers typically achieve 2–5 times faster drying rates compared to open sun drying and produce higher-quality dried products with lower moisture content and better colour. Reducing moisture content below 13% is critical for maize and pulses to prevent aflatoxin contamination, a major food safety and economic issue in the region.
applications: Vegetable and herb drying for market
Maize and grain drying to safe moisture levels
benefits: Faster drying reduces risk of mould and aflatoxin contamination
Protected drying improves product quality and marketability
Low technology and easy to fabricate locally
Works without electricity — uses passive solar heat
Reduces post-harvest losses and increases farmer income
limitations: Output depends on solar radiation and ambient humidity
Limited capacity per unit — multiple dryers needed for large volumes
Quality of local fabrication affects performance significantly
Not suitable for very wet or high-humidity conditions
Elevated plastic sheeting can degrade and needs replacing after 2–3 seasons
operationalNotes: Orient dryer north-south with collecting face angled to optimise solar capture
Do not overload trays — maintain thin layers of produce for even drying
Turn produce regularly for uniform drying
Use moisture meter to verify adequate drying before storage
Remove produce before evening to avoid reabsorption of moisture
maintenanceNotes: Inspect and replace plastic sheeting or glass cover annually
Check wooden/metal frame for structural integrity each season
Clean mesh trays after each drying cycle
Repaint exterior metal components annually to prevent rust
